title: The future with ḥa-: projects, invitations, appointments

blocks.text: With the present (EGY-03) and the past (EGY-04) tales; with the future organize. In Egyptian the future is very simple: ḥa- in front of the imperfect (ḥaktib (I shall write to the House) miš (miš ḥaktib). In this unit you use it to make projects, invite, accept and refuse with politeness, set an appointment: the situations that you will live every day in Cairo, and that prepare Luke's arrival in July. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-12, B1-13 and B1-14.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 119–124), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to form and deny the future with ḥa- and miš ḥa-;
2. expressing intentions (nāwi) and plans;
3. invite, accept and refuse in a courteous manner;
4. set a place, day and time for an appointment, and move it;
5. use future expressions of time (bukra, baʿd bukra, il-usbūʿ ig-gayy, kamān šuwayya).
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

chapters.title: 2. The Egyptian future and the fuṣḥā

blocks.text: ⁧لَنْ أُسَافِرَ⁩ miš ḥasāfir I won't leave.

ḥa- or has-? Cairo feels like it. ḥa- is ha- (with light h), especially in the fast talk: haktib, hanrūḥ. They're the same thing; in this course we write ḥa-. Future and present. As in English, the present with b- can indicate a near and planned future: bukra barūḥ il-gamʿa I'm going to college tomorrow. ḥa- stresses the intention or prediction.
The future is formed by ḥa- + simple imperfect (without b-).

Denial Is Always miš : miš ḥaktib I won't write, miš ḥanrūḥ We're not going. Never but...-š with the future. With the pronouns: ḥaʾullak I'll tell you, ḥašufak Bukra ... I see you tomorrow... ḥakallimha I'll call her.

Thanks, you give a reason (also vague: ʿandi mišwār I have a commission to do and it opens up to another occasion (marra tanya).
